questions.question: Consider the following statements about Article 5: 1. It requires domicile in India on the date of commencement of Constitution. 2. It requires either birth in India OR birth of either parent in India OR ordinary residence for 5 years. 3. Both conditions (domicile + one of the three) must be satisfied. Which are CORRECT?
Assertion (A): India does not recognise dual citizenship. Reason (R): Article 9 provides that voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship automatically ends Indian citizenship.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
Both are true but R does not explain A
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true ---

questions.question: Consider these statements about OCI: 1. OCI holders enjoy voting rights in local body elections. 2. OCI holders can hold the post of Chief Election Commissioner. 3. OCI holders need a visa to visit India. 4. OCI holders get lifelong multiple-entry visa. Which are CORRECT?
In the case of **Izhar Ahmad Khan v. Union of India (1962)**, the Supreme Court interpreted which Articles?

Consider statements about the CAA 2019: 1. It covers only Hindus from Pakistan, Afghanistan, Bangladesh. 2. It covers six religious minorities — Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi, Christian. 3. The cut-off date is December 31, 2014. 4. The applicants must have entered India legally. Which are CORRECT?
The constitutional challenge to CAA 2019 is primarily based on violation of:

Assertion (A): Articles 5–11 of the Constitution are of permanent nature. Reason (R): These Articles define citizenship at the commencement and leave all further regulation to Parliament under Article 11.

options.text: A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true
Both A and R are true
Both are false > Articles 5–11 are essentially transitional — they settled citizenship at commencement (Jan 26, 1950). Permanent regulation is by Parliament's law (Citizenship Act, 1955). ---

questions.question: Consider: A person was born in India in 1960. His father was born in undivided India (now Pakistan) in 1920. His mother was a foreign national. Is he an Indian citizen under Article 5?

options.text: Yes, because he was born in India

Yes, because his father was born in India
